Faqs.Q: What is the difference between cusped Mughal arches and classical Roman stone arches?
Faqs.A: Cusped Mughal arches (also known as multi-foil or scalloped arches) feature a series of rhythmic foliations radiating from a pointed center apex, representing classical Indo-Islamic palatial architecture. In contrast, classical Roman stone arches feature a continuous semicircular curve with uniform radial voussoirs. At Shree Ram & Company, our Jaipur atelier sculpts both traditional multi-cusped mehrabs with floral spandrels and sleek minimalist fluted arches designed for contemporary luxury residences.

Faqs.Q: How are heavy carved stone arches installed safely over door frames and hallways?
Faqs.A: Carved stone arches are installed using mechanical dry-cladding anchors and structural lintel tie-backs. Rather than placing unsupported vertical dead load onto wooden door frames or drywall, each stone arch segment (springer, voussoir, and keystone) is pre-grooved with rear slots. Grade-304/316 stainless steel brackets and threaded chemical anchors fasten each stone block directly into the structural RCC lintel or brick masonry, reinforced with high-tensile epoxy along interlocking joints.

Faqs.Q: What are the standard dimensions and customization options for prayer mehrabs?
Faqs.A: Traditional prayer mehrabs are fully custom-dimensioned to match ceiling heights, ranging from compact 5-foot residential niches to grand 14-foot community prayer halls. Standard wall depths range from 4 inches to 12 inches. Customizations include multi-layered tiered framing, integrated LED light channels along the arch rim, bas-relief Quranic calligraphy or floral arabesque spandrels, and integrated marble pilaster columns.

Faqs.Q: What is the cost per running foot or square foot for custom carved stone arches from Jaipur?
Faqs.A: The price of custom carved stone arches typically ranges from Rs 1,200 to Rs 3,800 per running foot for standard profiled stone door surrounds, or between Rs 1,800 to Rs 4,500 per square foot for deeply chiseled 3D cusped mehrabs with ornamental spandrels. Pricing depends on stone selection (Gwalior Mint vs Makrana White Marble), arch span, and whether the design requires monolithic or segmented stone carving.

Faqs.Q: What stone is best for outdoor entrance name plates in Indian climate?
Faqs.A: Natural Jet Black Granite and Bansi Paharpur Pink Sandstone are the two best stones for outdoor entrance name plates in India. Jet Black Granite has a Mohs hardness of 6.5 to 7 and zero porosity, creating maximum visual contrast against 24K gold foil or white engraved letters with zero fading under 48°C summer sun and torrential monsoon rain. Bansi Paharpur sandstone is ideal for heritage and contemporary earthy facades, providing an authentic palatial texture that never warps or deteriorates.

Faqs.Q: What Vastu guidelines should be followed for home entrance name plates?
Faqs.A: According to Vastu Shastra, an entrance name plate should be mounted on the right side of the main door (when looking from outside) at eye level (around 5 to 5.5 feet above finished ground level). The name plate must be well-lit, clearly legible, and free from dark obscuring shadows. The lettering must be crisp and clean, avoiding broken or chaotic fonts. Natural stones like granite, marble, and sandstone are highly auspicious in Vastu because they represent the grounding Earth element (Prithvi).

Faqs.Q: How are stone name plates fixed securely on boundary wall gates and exterior pillars?
Faqs.A: Stone name plates are fixed using concealed rear stainless steel studs and high-strength construction poly-epoxy. At our Jaipur factory, blind holes are drilled into the rear of the stone slab and fitted with threaded grade-304 SS rods. On site, matching holes are drilled into the stone, brick, or concrete pillar, injected with structural epoxy, and the name plate is pressed flush against the surface. This eliminates visible screws while ensuring the plate cannot be stolen or detached by wind.

Faqs.Q: What is the typical cost and lead time for a customized stone name plate from Jaipur?
Faqs.A: A custom handcrafted stone or granite name plate typically costs between Rs 3,500 to Rs 25,000+ depending on dimensions (e.g., standard 12x18 inch villa plate vs grand 36x24 inch estate plaque), stone grade, depth of relief carving, and whether gold leaf gilding or backlit acrylic backing is requested. Faqs.Q: How do natural sandstone garden articles withstand severe Indian weather and monsoon moisture?
Faqs.A: Rajasthan sandstones like Bansi Paharpur and Gwalior Mint have formed under millions of years of geological pressure, giving them exceptional silica quartz density and low porosity (<1.5%). When exposed to outdoor monsoons, high humidity, and winter temperatures, natural stone breathes without trapping internal hydrostatic moisture, completely preventing the spalling, flaking, or chemical cracking that ruins concrete or terracotta. Over decades, natural stone develops a rich, noble patina that enhances landscape beauty.

Faqs.Q: What drainage and planting considerations are needed for heavy carved stone planters?
Faqs.A: All carved stone planters manufactured by Shree Ram & Company feature precision center-core drainage apertures (typically 25mm–40mm diameter) to prevent root rot. We recommend lining the base with geotextile filter fabric and an inch of gravel before adding potting soil. Because natural stone is a superb thermal insulator, it keeps plant root balls significantly cooler during scorching 45°C summers compared to thin plastic or metal pots.

Faqs.Q: Can heavy stone benches and garden statues be installed on terrace gardens and balconies?
Faqs.A: Yes, provided the structural load-bearing capacity of the terrace slab is verified. A standard 4-foot carved sandstone bench weighs approximately 120 kg to 180 kg, while a decorative stone planter ranges from 40 kg to 90 kg. For rooftop terraces, our engineers design modular hollow-core assemblies or distribute base plinths over structural beam lines to ensure dead load stays well within standard residential slab limits (300–450 kg/m²).

Faqs.Q: What is the pricing and delivery process for stone garden articles across India?
Faqs.A: Handcrafted stone garden articles typically range from Rs 4,500 for compact birdbaths and lantern pedestals to Rs 85,000+ for large 6-foot carved estate benches and monolithic tree planters. Each item is pre-assembled, water-tested (for fountains and birdbaths), and packed inside heavy-duty foam-lined wooden crates. Faqs.Q: What civil foundation and concrete slab are required before installing a stone gazebo?
Faqs.A: A stone gazebo imposes significant static dead load—typically between 6 to 25 metric tons depending on the diameter (e.g., 8-foot private gazebo vs 18-foot grand community pavilion). Installation requires a reinforced concrete (RCC) raft slab of 6 to 9 inches thickness, cast with grade M25 concrete, and reinforced with a double grid of 10mm or 12mm TMT steel bars. At Shree Ram & Company, our Jaipur architectural team provides structural foundation load drawings and column anchor-bolt schematics prior to manufacturing.

Faqs.Q: How are the dome and pillars of a stone gazebo assembled safely on site?
Faqs.A: Stone gazebos are erected using traditional mortise-and-tenon compression joints augmented with modern stainless steel dowel pins. The base plinth is leveled first with high-strength non-shrink grout. Each monolithic pillar is pinned vertically into the foundation slab via central 25mm SS rods. Heavy carved architrave beams bridge the columns, after which the corbelled stone dome rings are set concentric layer by layer until the self-locking keystone and kalash finial are lowered into place.

Faqs.Q: How do natural sandstone gazebos perform against monsoons, windstorms, and extreme sun?
Faqs.A: Natural Rajasthan sandstone gazebos are virtually impervious to harsh environmental factors. Unlike wood (which rots, warps, and suffers termite damage) or metal (which rusts and overheats in the summer sun), natural sandstone is fireproof, termite-immune, and acts as a natural thermal buffer that keeps interior seating comfortably cool. Due to its massive dead load and aerodynamic dome profile, a properly anchored stone gazebo can withstand hurricane-force wind gusts exceeding 160 km/h.

Faqs.A: A custom handcrafted stone gazebo typically costs between Rs 3,50,000 to Rs 18,00,000+ depending on overall diameter (8ft, 12ft, 16ft+), number of pillars (4, 6, 8, or 12 columns), and the density of ornamental 3D relief carving across pillars, arches, and dome ceilings. Faqs.Q: How can I verify genuine handcrafted Makrana marble handicrafts versus machine-molded resin?
Faqs.A: Genuine Makrana marble handicrafts have distinct characteristics that machine-made plastic or resin copies cannot replicate. Natural marble feels noticeably cold to the touch and rings with a clear acoustic chime when tapped gently with a metal coin. Under magnification, you will see subtle natural crystalline calcite veining rather than uniform plastic perfection. Furthermore, genuine stone pieces have natural weight (2.7 g/cm³ density) and will never melt, discolor, or emit chemical smells when exposed to lit tea-light candles or burning camphor.

Faqs.Q: What are the best ways to care for and clean handcrafted marble urlis and lanterns?
Faqs.A: Handcrafted marble urlis used for floating flowers and floating candles should be emptied and wiped dry every 3 to 4 days to prevent mineral water rings. Clean with lukewarm water and a drop of neutral liquid soap using a soft cotton sponge. Avoid acidic toilet cleansers, lemon juice, or abrasive scouring pads. For delicate openwork jali lanterns with candle soot, use a soft baby toothbrush dipped in mild soapy water to gently reach carved crevices.

Faqs.Q: Do you provide custom corporate gifting and bulk packaging for stone handicrafts?
Faqs.A: Yes, Shree Ram & Company specializes in bespoke corporate gifts, VIP wedding favors, and architectural presentation pieces. We offer custom laser-engraved corporate branding, brass commemorative plates, and luxury velvet-lined presentation boxes. We accommodate production volumes from small exclusive runs of 20 pieces to large exports of 2,000+ units with guaranteed quality consistency.

Faqs.Q: How are delicate openwork stone handicrafts packaged for safe domestic and international transit?

Faqs.Q: What is authentic Mughal Pietra Dura marble inlay and what gemstones are used?
Faqs.A: Authentic Mughal Pietra Dura (known locally as Parchin Kari) is a heritage lapidary art where slivers of genuine semi-precious gemstones are hand-cut and embedded into pre-chiseled cavities in solid marble slabs. Originating in Renaissance Florence and perfected in 17th-century Mughal Agra and Jaipur, this art uses real gemstones including Lapis Lazuli (deep blue), Malachite (banded green), Carnelian (fiery orange), Jasper (earthy red and brown), Turquoise (sky blue), Mother of Pearl (iridescent shell), and Tiger Eye. When completed, the stones sit 100% flush with the marble matrix, creating a lifetime permanent mosaic that never fades or detaches.

Faqs.Q: How do you distinguish genuine gemstone marble inlay from synthetic resin imitation?
Faqs.A: Genuine Pietra Dura marble inlay can be verified by touching and inspecting the gemstone surface. Natural gemstones are cool to the touch and exhibit natural internal geological striations, mineral inclusions, and variable depth of color. In contrast, synthetic imitations use tinted polyester resin or colored stone dust mixed with epoxy, which feels warm/plastic-like, lacks natural crystalline fire, and shows tiny trapped air bubbles under a loupe. Furthermore, genuine stone inlay will not scratch when tested with a standard brass edge, whereas plastic resin scratches easily.

Faqs.Q: How should marble inlay dining tables and floor medallions be cleaned and maintained?
Faqs.A: Marble inlay surfaces should be cleaned using a clean microfiber cloth dampened with lukewarm water or neutral pH stone wash. Never use acidic cleaning solutions, vinegar, lemon juice, or abrasive powders, as acid attacks the calcium carbonate of the marble and the natural luster of semi-precious stones. Spills of wine, coffee, or turmeric should be wiped away promptly. For periodic enhancement, applying a thin coat of natural carnauba wax or neutral stone polish restores radiant depth without building up yellow residue.

Faqs.Q: What is the cost per square foot for bespoke marble inlay work from Jaipur?
Faqs.A: The cost of authentic handcrafted Pietra Dura marble inlay typically ranges from Rs 2,500 to Rs 12,000+ per square foot depending on gemstone selection and floral motif density. A subtle border inlay with Mother of Pearl and Carnelian in Makrana marble starts around Rs 2,500 to Rs 4,500 per sq ft. Complex, museum-grade floral bouquets and central medallions utilizing rare Lapis Lazuli, Malachite, and Turquoise with hundreds of hand-cut petals per square foot range between Rs 6,500 and Rs 15,000+ per sq ft. Complete custom dining tables (6-seater to 12-seater) range from Rs 1,25,000 to Rs 8,50,000+.

Faqs.Q: How do you protect marble dining table tops from food stains, wine, and acidic etching?
Faqs.A: Natural marble is calcium-based and susceptible to acidic etching from lemon juice, vinegar, alcohol, and turmeric if left unprotected. At Shree Ram & Company, every marble table top undergoes a multi-layer deep-penetrating nano-sealing treatment prior to dispatch. This food-grade fluorochemical barrier penetrates into the micro-pores of the stone, repelling liquids without altering the stone's natural color or cool silky touch. For daily maintenance, spills should be blotted with a damp microfiber cloth, and hot pans should be placed on coasters or trivets.

Faqs.Q: What base structure and weight capacity are required to support a solid marble table top?
Faqs.A: A standard 20mm thick solid marble table top weighs approximately 55 kg per square meter (around 110 kg for a 6-seater dining table), while a 30mm slab weighs nearly 85 kg/m². Supporting bases—whether fabricated from solid teakwood, cast brass, stainless steel, or carved stone pedestals—must feature an intermediate sub-base (such as a 19mm marine-grade plywood or steel perimeter frame) that distributes dead weight evenly and prevents stress concentration along the marble center.

Faqs.Q: What custom shapes, edge profiles, and sizes can be ordered from Jaipur?
Faqs.A: We fabricate 100% bespoke marble tops to your exact architectural specifications. Popular shapes include racetrack oval, soft rectangular, round circular (from 36-inch coffee tables to 72-inch banquet rounds), pill shape, and boat-neck executive tables. Edge profile options include modern shark-nose (knife-edge), subtle chamfer, full bullnose, half bullnose, and ornate classical double ogee.

Faqs.Q: How are heavy marble table tops packaged and delivered safely without cracking?
Faqs.A: Marble slabs are highly rigid but vulnerable to bending during transit. We package each tabletop inside a custom-built, ISPM-15 export-compliant wooden A-frame crate. The marble is wrapped in multi-layer EPE foam, corner-cushioned with impact-absorbing blocks, and strapped vertically on edge—the only structurally safe orientation for transporting natural stone slabs. We provide fully insured door-to-door transit across all Indian metro cities.

Faqs.Q: What is HDMR board and why is it superior to standard MDF for interior wall paneling?
Faqs.A: HDMR stands for High Density Moisture Resistant board. Unlike standard MDF (which has a density around 650–700 kg/m³ and swells when exposed to humidity), HDMR is engineered with a density exceeding 850–900 kg/m³ using specialized synthetic resin binders. This higher fiber density gives HDMR superior screw-holding strength, excellent moisture resistance in air-conditioned environments, and clean, fuzz-free edges during detailed CNC routing that achieve a flawless automotive-grade PU paint finish.

Faqs.Q: How are 3D CNC fluted HDMR wall panels mounted securely on interior masonry walls?
Faqs.A: HDMR wall panels are mounted using an interlocking French cleat or aluminum Z-clip sub-frame system. A calibrated plywood or wooden framework (12mm–18mm) is first anchored to the brick or concrete wall using nylon expansion fasteners, creating an air gap that prevents moisture transfer from the masonry. The pre-finished CNC HDMR panels, fitted with matching reverse cleats on their back, lock securely into the sub-frame without any visible screw holes or nails on the decorative front face.

Faqs.Q: What paint and polishing options work best on CNC carved HDMR surfaces?
Faqs.A: The ideal finish for CNC carved HDMR is multi-coat Polyurethane (PU) paint applied in a controlled dust-free spray booth. The process involves two coats of high-build polyester/PU primer to seal the routed fibers, thorough sanding to 400-grit smoothness, followed by two coats of premium Italian PU topcoat (available in deep matte, satin 20% sheen, or 100% high-gloss buffed finish). PU coatings provide a waterproof, scratch-resistant, and non-yellowing surface that retains its luster for decades.

Faqs.Q: What is the cost per square foot for custom CNC 3D HDMR wall paneling?
Faqs.A: The cost of custom CNC 3D HDMR wall paneling typically ranges between Rs 280 to Rs 850 per square foot in India. Standard 2D fluted or reeded patterns in 12mm–18mm HDMR board (unpainted or primer-coated) range from Rs 280 to Rs 450 per sq ft. Complex 3D organic wave panels or geometric parametric designs with professional spray-booth PU duco finish range from Rs 550 to Rs 950+ per sq ft, depending on panel thickness and finish specification.

Faqs.Q: Is HDMR jali suitable for pooja room doors and living room room dividers?
Faqs.A: Yes, HDMR is one of the most popular and versatile materials for interior pooja room doors and living room dividers. Because of its dense uniform matrix (>850 kg/m³), it can be intricately routed into sacred Om, Swastika, Lotus, and traditional Indian lattice designs without splintering. When finished with a high-quality PU coating or metallic brass/gold leafing, HDMR jali creates a luxurious, warm architectural screen that complements both modern and traditional home decor.

Faqs.Q: How should intricate laser/CNC cut MDF jalis be prepped and spray-painted?
Faqs.A: To ensure a smooth, professional finish on intricate CNC-cut jalis, proper surface preparation is critical. First, routed edges are hand-sanded with 220-grit paper to remove any residual micro-fibers. A high-penetrating PU or polyurethane wood sealer is sprayed to seal the porous cut edges, followed by two coats of high-build PU surfacer primer. After fine sanding to 400-grit, automotive-grade PU paint (Duco or Polyurethane) is spray-applied in thin, uniform coats to prevent paint pooling inside small lattice perforations.

Faqs.Q: What thickness of MDF/HDMR should be chosen for freestanding room partition screens?
Faqs.A: For freestanding or floor-to-ceiling room partition screens, 18mm or 25mm thickness is strongly recommended. Thin 8mm–12mm boards lack structural rigidity over tall spans (above 6 feet) and will flex or bow under air pressure or incidental contact. For screens taller than 7 feet, we fabricate a solid 25mm to 35mm thick outer boundary frame with internal 18mm jali fretwork to ensure absolute vertical stability.

Faqs.Q: What lighting design best accentuates the 3D relief texture of a carved stone mural?
Faqs.A: To fully highlight the depth and shadow play of a 3D stone carving, grazing light (raking light) is the gold standard. Install warm white (2700K–3000K) recessed ceiling spotlights or linear LED wall grazers positioned 6 to 12 inches away from the wall surface, angled downward at a steep 15°–25° angle. This steep angle casts dramatic micro-shadows behind undercut petals, mythological figures, and textures, creating an ethereal three-dimensional presence in the room.

Faqs.Q: How do I choose between natural sandstone, WPC, and HDMR for my room partition jali?

HDMR is ideal for dry interior living-dining separators and bedroom screens where delicate geometric fretwork and automotive PU lacquer finishes are needed. WPC composite is best for semi-covered balconies, bathroom dividers, and exterior terraces because it is 100% waterproof and termite-proof.

Faqs.Q: How are tall floor-to-ceiling partition screens installed without damaging finished flooring?
Faqs.A: For luxury interiors with finished Italian marble or hardwood flooring, we utilize a specialized perimeter U-channel framing system with high-tensile silicone structural adhesives or concealed pressure jacks. The outer frame is secured into the concrete ceiling slab above, while the bottom channel sits on an elastomeric neoprene vibration pad adhered with neutral-cure structural silicone. This holds the screen rigidly in place against wind and human contact without drilling invasive anchor holes into expensive floor marble.

Faqs.Q: What perforation percentage is best for balancing visual privacy and natural light flow?
Faqs.A: The optimal perforation ratio for residential partition screens ranges between 35% and 50% open area. An open area of 35% to 40% provides high visual privacy (obscuring direct line of sight between dining and living areas) while casting decorative shadows under ambient light. A 45% to 55% open area is ideal for corridors, foyer dividers, and staircases where maximum light throughput and free air circulation are desired.

Faqs.Q: What is the difference between solid load-bearing stone pillars and hollow cladding pillars?
Faqs.A: Solid stone pillars are carved from a single monolithic block of natural sandstone or marble and are capable of carrying direct structural dead and live loads from roof beams and upper floors (compressive strength >60 MPa). In contrast, hollow cladding pillars (also called split or modular column wraps) are manufactured in two semicircular halves or 3-part segments designed to wrap around an existing reinforced concrete (RCC) column or structural steel I-beam. Cladding pillars provide the identical regal aesthetic of solid stone while allowing seamless retrofitting around structural building frameworks.

Faqs.Q: What classical architectural proportions are used for Jaipur carved stone columns?
Faqs.A: Our master Sompura carvers follow classical architectural orders derived from the Manasara and Shilpa Shastra. A traditional stone column is divided into three harmonious sections: the Adhisthana (base plinth, typically 1/5th total height), the Stambha (shaft, typically 3/5th total height, available in octagonal-to-round fluted taper), and the Shirsha (carved bracket capital, typically 1/5th total height, featuring carved elephants, lotus petals, or classical scrolls). Standard diameter-to-height ratios range from 1:6 for sturdy heritage porticos to 1:8 for graceful interior colonnades.

Faqs.Q: How are heavy stone pillars anchored safely to concrete foundations and roof beams?
Faqs.A: Solid stone pillars are anchored using concealed vertical central dowel pins forged from grade-316 stainless steel (typically 25mm to 32mm diameter). The pin is embedded 150mm into the concrete foundation slab with non-shrink structural epoxy grout and extends 150mm upward into a pre-drilled core hole in the base of the stone shaft. A matching top dowel pin locks the capital securely into the overhead beam, eliminating any possibility of horizontal shear movement during seismic events or high winds.

Faqs.Q: What is the cost and delivery lead time for custom carved stone pillars from Jaipur?
Faqs.A: Custom carved stone pillars typically cost between Rs 18,000 to Rs 1,20,000+ per column depending on total height (e.g., 7ft residential vs 14ft monumental), shaft diameter (8 inches to 18 inches), stone grade, and the complexity of capital carving. Production time in our Jaipur atelier takes approximately 3 to 5 weeks. Pillars are pre-fitted, numbered, wrapped in protective foam, and shipped in reinforced wooden crates with nationwide door-to-site delivery.

Faqs.Q: What relief depth is typical for a 3D stone mural, and how does it affect the visual impact?
Faqs.A: Stone relief murals are typically categorized into low relief (Bas-Relief: 15mm–25mm depth), medium relief (Mezzo-Relief: 30mm–50mm depth), and high relief (Alto-Relief: 50mm–100mm depth). Greater relief depth allows our sculptors to undercut features like tree branches, peacock feathers, and deity garments so they cast real shadow play on the background stone. In grand double-height spaces, high-relief carving ensures the artwork remains crisp and visually commanding even when viewed from 30 feet away.

Edge seams are cut along natural contour lines (such as tree branches or architectural borders) rather than straight geometric cuts. On site, panels are dry-fitted with matching stone-dust epoxy adhesive tinted to the exact mineral shade of the stone, rendering joint lines virtually invisible.

Faqs.Q: Can stone art murals be installed outdoors on boundary walls and exposed garden courtyards?

Natural sandstone does not deteriorate under ultraviolet sunlight, monsoon deluge, or winter frost. Exterior murals receive a breathable hydrophobic impregnating sealant that prevents rainwater absorption, moss growth, and dirt buildup while allowing the stone to breathe naturally.

Faqs.Q: What wall substructure is required to safely support heavy 3D stone wall panels?
Faqs.A: Natural stone wall panels (typically 25mm to 35mm thick) weigh approximately 55 kg to 75 kg per square meter. For solid brick masonry or RCC concrete walls, panels can be fixed using high-tensile polymer-modified cementitious tile adhesives (Class C2TE S1) combined with mechanical stainless steel anchor pins. For lightweight drywall partitions (gypsum or cement fiber board), an internal structural framework of heavy-gauge galvanised steel studs (at 300mm centers) with concealed French cleat brackets is required to support the dead load safely.

Faqs.Q: How are continuous textured wave and flute patterns aligned across multiple stone panels?
Faqs.A: Every continuous textured panel project at Shree Ram & Company is manufactured as a coordinated CAD batch. Large natural stone slabs are precision-cut into modular tiles, labeled sequentially on the rear, and machined in numerical order on our computerized 5-axis CNC router. This ensures that the peak of every wave and the groove of every flute transfers seamlessly across tile seams with zero dimensional mismatch.

Faqs.Q: Do natural stone wall panels offer acoustic and thermal insulation benefits for interiors?
Faqs.A: Yes, natural stone is an outstanding thermal and acoustic dampening material. Due to its high mass and irregular 3D textured relief surfaces, stone panels diffuse and break up sound waves, significantly reducing echo and reverberation in large double-height living rooms and hard-surface foyers. Thermally, natural sandstone's high thermal inertia buffers interior rooms against exterior temperature swings, maintaining a comfortable ambient microclimate.

Faqs.Q: What is the price range per square foot for 3D textured stone wall panels in India?
Faqs.A: The cost of 3D textured stone wall panels typically ranges between Rs 850 to Rs 2,800 per square foot in India. Standard linear fluted or grooved texture panels in Gwalior Mint or Teakwood Sandstone range from Rs 850 to Rs 1,400 per sq ft. Complex 3D multi-directional wave patterns, convex faceted panels, and deeply chiseled stone relief tiles range from Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,800+ per sq ft, depending on stone grade and relief depth.

Faqs.Q: What is the difference between dry-hanging mechanical cladding and wet mortar fixing?
Faqs.A: Dry-hanging mechanical cladding uses stainless steel (grade 304 or 316) brackets and anchor bolts to suspend stone panels from the structural wall, creating an insulated air cavity (typically 25mm–50mm) between the stone and the masonry. This cavity allows natural air ventilation, facilitates drainage of any incidental moisture, and accommodates thermal expansion without cracking. Wet mortar fixing attaches tiles directly to masonry using cement mortar or adhesive; while suitable for smaller tiles under 300x600mm, dry cladding is the engineering standard for exterior heights and heavy stone panels.

Faqs.Q: How does natural stone wall cladding prevent water seepage, dampness, and white efflorescence?
Faqs.A: Natural sandstone wall cladding acts as an external rain-screen shield that prevents driving monsoon rain from penetrating the core brickwork. In dry cladding systems, the ventilated air gap prevents moisture from reaching the inner wall. At Shree Ram & Company, all exterior stone cladding is treated with a breathable siloxane hydrophobic penetrating sealant that repels liquid water while allowing water vapor to escape, completely eliminating the unsightly white salt stains (efflorescence) common in unsealed masonry.

Faqs.Q: Does stone cladding provide thermal insulation to reduce air conditioning costs?
Faqs.A: Yes. Natural sandstone possesses high volumetric heat capacity (thermal mass). During peak summer afternoons when exterior temperatures reach 42°C–48°C, the stone cladding absorbs solar radiation slowly, delaying heat transmission into the building envelope by up to 6 to 8 hours. By the time heat reaches the inner wall, the outside air has cooled in the evening. This natural thermal lag significantly reduces interior heat gain and lowers residential air conditioning power consumption by up to 20%–30%.

Faqs.Q: What is the cost per square foot for exterior natural stone wall cladding in India?
Faqs.A: The cost of natural stone wall cladding in India typically ranges from Rs 180 to Rs 850 per square foot. Standard split-face sandstone strips and ledge-stone tiles range from Rs 180 to Rs 350 per sq ft. Calibrated large-format sandstone panels (600x1200mm) with grooved profiles range from Rs 380 to Rs 650 per sq ft. Complete turnkey dry-cladding systems (including stone, SS304 bracket hardware, anchor fasteners, and installation labor) range between Rs 650 and Rs 1,200 per sq ft.

Faqs.Q: Why is WPC jali better than MDF or PVC for exterior balconies and wet areas?
Faqs.A: WPC (Wood Polymer Composite) blends fine wood fibers with high-density thermoplastics (PVC/PE) and specialized UV stabilizers, creating an engineered board with zero water absorption (<0.2%). Unlike MDF (which swells and disintegrates when exposed to rain) and cheap PVC foam sheets (which soften and warp under direct 45°C summer sun), WPC possesses high structural stiffness (density 0.65–0.70 g/cm³), complete termite immunity, and superior thermal stability, making it the premier choice for exterior architectural screens.

Faqs.Q: How does WPC composite jali hold up under extreme Indian sun and monsoon rain?
Faqs.A: High-density WPC boards used by Shree Ram & Company are formulated with titanium dioxide and UV-inhibiting additives that prevent polymer brittleness and ultraviolet photodegradation. In regions with heavy monsoon downpours and high coastal humidity, WPC will never absorb water, rot, breed mold, or warp. For painted applications, we use exterior-grade polyurethane (PU) coatings with automotive cross-linking agents that maintain vibrant color for over 10 to 15 years.

Faqs.Q: What thickness of WPC board should be selected for exterior building duct screens?
Faqs.A: For exterior building duct coverings and balcony elevations subject to wind loads, an 18mm or 25mm thickness is strongly recommended. Boards thinner than 12mm lack the bending stiffness required to span across 4 to 8 foot structural openings and may flutter during storms. For extra-large vertical duct spans, panels are mounted within a heavy-gauge aluminum or galvanised iron (GI) perimeter box frame (50x25mm or 50x50mm) to ensure absolute structural safety.

Faqs.Q: How are WPC jali screens fixed and painted on outdoor balcony railings and facade frames?
Faqs.A: WPC jali screens are installed by framing them within an aluminum, MS, or wooden U-channel perimeter track and securing them with stainless steel countersunk screws. For painting, WPC requires a solvent-based plastic primer (such as an epoxy or polyurethane tie-coat) to ensure strong adhesion to the polymer surface. Once primed, two coats of exterior PU enamel or automotive Duco paint are spray-applied in your desired color, resulting in a smooth, weatherproof satin or gloss finish.
